mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has risen for two consecutive weeks (-55.0 to -50.1), indicating a resumption of commuting and weekday foot traffic near offices, which should feed through to higher retail and recreation visits over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved from -55.0 at t-2w to -50.1 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise (mean next 28 days <= mean last 28 days) despite WORKPLACES continuing to improve week-on-week over the forecast window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp week-on-week drop in PARKS mobility (-40.1 to -52.1 over two weeks) signals reduced outdoor activity substitution, consistent with people retreating indoors due to cold weather or renewed caution, which should coincide with continued suppression of RETAIL_REC.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls more than 5 points week-on-week for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS dropped from -40.1 at t-2w to -52.1 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days even though PARKS continues to decline sharply, invalidating the shared-suppression mechanism.

mechanism_narrative: When both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT rise together, it signals synchronized reopening momentum (commuting plus transit usage), which jointly drives higher RETAIL_REC through combined commute-linked and errand-linked trips, exceeding what either series alone would predict.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both rise by at least 2 points over the same two-week window
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose from -55.0 to -50.1 while TRANSIT stayed roughly flat near -60
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise even when both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT rise concurrently for two or more weeks, showing no interaction effect.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility remaining persistently elevated above +15 points indicates households are still spending disproportionate time at home, a stay-at-home behavioral regime that caps discretionary retail and recreation trips regardless of other signals.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL remains above +15 points for all four snapshot weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL stayed between 17.1 and 18.0 across all four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 28 days while RESIDENTIAL remains elevated above +15, contradicting the suppression mechanism.

mechanism_narrative: The steady decline in PARKS mobility reflects a seasonal shift away from outdoor recreation (e.g., cooling temperatures), which should redirect some recreational demand toward indoor retail and recreation venues, modestly lifting RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS declines for two consecutive weeks while RETAIL_REC does not decline further
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell from -40.1 to -52.1 while RETAIL_REC stabilized from -66.6 to -66.1
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to decline in tandem with PARKS rather than showing the hypothesized substitution effect.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT mobility fails to recover even as WORKPLACES mobility improves, this divergence suggests persistent transit-capacity policy constraints (e.g., reduced service, distancing rules) that cap commute-linked retail trips, limiting RETAIL_REC growth despite workplace reopening.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises by more than 3 points week-on-week while TRANSIT changes by less than 1 point in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose ~4.9 points from t-2w to t-0w while TRANSIT changed only ~2.2 points and non-monotonically
regime_hint: constrained reopening under transit policy limits
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises strongly even though TRANSIT remains flat or declining while WORKPLACES improves, disproving the policy-cap mechanism.

mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC's own recent uptick from -66.6 to -66.1 after three weeks of decline suggests a bottoming-out or mean-reversion pattern, implying the series is poised for a mild rebound over the next week.
candidate_trigger: RETAIL_REC rises week-on-week after at least two prior weeks of decline
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved slightly from -66.6 at t-1w to -66.1 at t-0w after declining in prior weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to decline in the week immediately following the observed uptick, contradicting the mean-reversion signal.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous plateau in RESIDENTIAL (slight decline from 18.0 to 17.3) alongside stable GROCERY_PHARM mobility indicates early-stage normalization of daily routines, which together should precede a modest rise in RETAIL_REC as discretionary trips resume.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL declines for two consecutive weeks while GROCERY_PHARM remains within a 3-point band
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell from 18.0 to 17.3 while GROCERY_PHARM stayed between -35.7 and -32.7
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise even as RESIDENTIAL declines and GROCERY_PHARM stabilizes, indicating no joint normalization effect.
